recap.text: Carl finds Toyotomi, a bipedal rhinoceros, duct-taped in a castle after Donut tried to swallow his foot. Toyotomi joins the Princess Posse and leads Li Na's builders in Shanty Town to construct the Nest, a granite synergy tower. While guarding Donut in the Nest, Toyotomi reports a woman with a dog entering the tower. Carl finds Toyotomi and his mages cleaved in half by a spell.

beats.headline: He ate my boot
beats.text: For the record: found duct-taped in the Prism's castle, with Crawler Carl's pet attempting to swallow his foot. A large bipedal rhinoceros, a true NPC, now under a Princess Posse banner. He frees his wrists and moves to clobber the pet. He ate my boot, he reports; one boot is gone, revealing a round foot. Carl apologizes and promises a replacement. Toyotomi. Level 70 Sai Outpost Guard Mercenary Leader. Sergeant in the Princess Posse. A hired mercenary, paid to the end of the floor or his death, inherited when the Prism fell.
beats.gist: Carl finds Toyotomi, a rhinoceros mercenary, duct-taped in the Prism's castle while Carl's pet swallows his foot.

beats.headline: A broken creature, per the file
beats.text: The System's file on the subject. Once an honorable, experienced leader of Sai. His entire squad died in an incident at the Desperado Club that Crawler Carl may or may not have been partially responsible for, and the few survivors went to the mercenary markets. His failure to protect his friends against the demon haunts him, and he refuses to lead men now, despite great talent. He was regaining his confidence when a man in underwear and a talking cat trounced him, tied him up and slaughtered his charge.
beats.gist: Sergeant Toyotomi is a Sai mercenary whose squad died at the Desperado Club.

beats.headline: Accepting his exile
beats.text: His magic is for outposts, not palaces. Edifice Shield cannot cover a castle bigger than this one, and this one was already too big; Warlord D'Nadia insisted, so he shielded it in spurts, and was resting when the crawlers arrived. I am shamed. Leave him here, he asks, to defend this building until he dies. It is what he wants. Carl changes the plan and sends him to Shanty Town. He accepts his exile. It is not an exile, Carl says. They need his talents.
beats.gist: Carl sends Sergeant Toyotomi to Shanty Town because they need his talents for outposts.

beats.headline: Leader of Li Na's builders
beats.text: Earlier, at the foot of Li Na's new clocktower in Shanty Town, the subject was seen pointing up and talking animatedly, in his element, directing the last-minute construction. Now dozens of wires dangle from the clocktower's arms, an exploit; if it works, Li Na's builder squad, led by the subject, gets straight to work on a very tall, very powerful, very specialized and very expensive synergy tower at the edge of the hole leading down into Larracos. It only works during the next phase. In the menu, its name is simple. It is called the Nest.
beats.gist: Sergeant Toyotomi leads Li Na's builders to construct the Nest synergy tower at the Larracos hole.

beats.headline: It is the color of granite
beats.text: The Nest is up, and Crawler Donut wants it purple. It is the color of granite, the subject answers, because it is made of granite; paint it now and the mages cannot coat it in protections, and if the build is master quality it glows gold. The protections: at least twenty per block by bleed and net pattern, strength to two hundred percent on completion, doubled by his Edifice Shield. Four deflector towers where one would do. Carl asks, for the third time, about tunneling. It is protected enough to float if the ground disappears.
beats.gist: Sergeant Toyotomi tells Crawler Donut the Nest is granite and cannot be painted.

beats.headline: Deflector towers keep the gods away
beats.text: Crawler Donut relays the subject's professional opinion to Carl over the chat: Toyotomi says the deflector towers keep the gods away. Carl advises her to think of them as an electric fence. They are far from foolproof. She should avoid unnecessary god attention, which means not shrieking over a massive PA. She does not shriek, she says.
beats.gist: Donut relays Toyotomi's opinion that deflector towers keep gods away; Carl compares them to electric fences.

beats.headline: A woman with a dog
beats.text: The last messages from the Nest's lower floor, where the subject stands guard over Crawler Donut with Bomo and several mages. Bomo: someone is trying to come into the tower. Toyotomi: he is securing the front entrance. Donut: she cannot leave the tower; there is a net around it. Carl asks if it is one of the zarogoth things. No, the subject answers. It is a crawler. A woman with a dog. She's coming in. System note on that message: This message is from a deceased mercenary.
beats.gist: Sergeant Toyotomi stands guard over Crawler Donut with Bomo and mages before a system note marks him deceased.

beats.headline: Toyotomi was dead-dead
beats.text: Crawler Carl reaches the Nest and spares a quick, sad glance for the subject, Bomo and the defending mages, all of them cleaved in half with a spell. Bomo is supposed to regenerate on the tenth floor. Toyotomi is not. Toyotomi was dead-dead. Up the curving stairwell, Lucia Mar is shouting at her dog.
beats.gist: Carl reaches the Nest and sees Toyotomi, Bomo, and defending mages cleaved in half.
